intro.vo: Movement two. D major, Allegretto ma non troppo. After the violence of the first movement, this arrives like a door opening onto a different world , bright, hushed, and seemingly serene. But the serenity is not stable. From its very first phrase the harmony begins pulling flatward, away from D major and toward a darker chromatic orbit. The movement will not end in D major. It will end on a chord that belongs to no key, and the next movement will begin before the silence can settle. What you are about to hear is a journey out and a journey back, and the return is not a resolution.

cues.label: Cello opens alone
cues.vo_pre: The cello enters alone. No other instrument plays. This is four full measures of a single unaccompanied voice before the quartet has even assembled.
cues.vo_post: That bare cello line descends through the D major scale and arrives on A, the fifth of the key, the note of maximum tension. No chord, no harmony, just a scale announcing the tonal world through its shape rather than its sound. No Beethoven quartet movement opens this way.

cues.label: Ensemble enters, harmony pulls flatward
cues.vo_pre: The full ensemble enters. Listen to where the harmony immediately moves , not where you might expect.
cues.vo_post: The opening chord is built on D, the home key, but with a note borrowed from outside it, turning the chord into a signpost pointing toward G minor. And that is exactly where it resolves. The movement's defining gesture appears in its very first phrase: D major, immediately leaning toward its darker neighbour.

cues.label: Two chromatic shock chords
cues.vo_pre: Two short, sharp chords are about to cut through the D major flow. They last a single beat each.
cues.vo_post: Those two chords are the most harmonically dense moment in the movement so far. All four inner voices move up by a single semitone from the first to the second, a chain reaction in the smallest possible interval. Then D major returns as if nothing happened. These chords will come back.

cues.label: Viola launches the contrasting section alone
cues.vo_pre: The viola takes over as soloist, alone, beginning a new section. This mirrors exactly what the cello did at the opening.
cues.vo_post: The viola opens with the same descending half step the cello used to begin the movement, D to C sharp. But where the cello turned toward the fifth, the viola turns flatward immediately. C natural, B flat , notes that pull the harmony away from D major toward the darker regions it has been hinting at since measure five.

cues.label: Flat-side extreme, cello pedal, diminished chord
cues.vo_pre: The music is about to reach its furthest point from D major. Listen for the cello holding a single note in the bass while the harmony above it darkens to its limit.
cues.vo_post: The cello holds E flat for four full measures while the first violin reaches D flat six, as remote from D major as it is possible to get. The passage closes on a fully diminished seventh chord , four notes each a minor third apart, producing maximum harmonic tension. Then a single pivot chord connects to what follows.

cues.label: Chromatic cello descent, structural centre
cues.vo_pre: The cello is alone again. This time its descent is not a diatonic scale but a fully chromatic line, moving almost entirely by half steps across twelve measures.
cues.vo_post: This is the structural centre of the movement. The cello descends from A flat, the pitch a tritone away from D, down through nearly every semitone within a minor seventh span. The violins enter briefly above it, adding flat-side colour before withdrawing. The line ends on A, the dominant of D major, but arrives there from the far side of the harmonic universe.

cues.label: Viola completes the harmony, one note
cues.vo_pre: At the very end of the cello descent, listen for the viola entering on a single note.
cues.vo_post: Without the viola, the chord is incomplete , the dominant of D major with its fifth missing. The viola supplies exactly that note, closing the chord and completing twelve measures of harmonic wandering. One instrument, one pitch, turning an open question into an answer.

cues.label: Viola launches the return, mirror of measure 35
cues.vo_pre: The viola launches alone again, the same mechanism as measure 35. But listen to the direction.
cues.vo_post: At measure 35 the viola opened on D and turned flatward. Now it opens on B flat, the last echo of that flat world, and the violin enters immediately turning sharply back toward D major. The same solo-launch mechanism, the harmonic direction completely reversed. The outward journey is over.

cues.label: Reprise seam on a single note
cues.vo_pre: The cello's D at measure 112 is two things at once. Listen for how quickly it moves.
cues.vo_post: That D closes the return section and immediately continues to C sharp, launching a note-for-note reprise of the opening cello solo. The structural seam falls on a single note rather than between measures. Arrival and departure share the same downbeat.

cues.label: Reprise an octave higher, shock chords return
cues.vo_pre: The full ensemble returns with the opening theme. Listen for the register , and then listen for those two sharp chords when they arrive.
cues.vo_post: The theme follows the same harmonic path as the opening, measure by measure, but sits an octave higher throughout. And the two chromatic shock chords return at measures 134 and 135, exactly as they appeared at measures 23 and 24. Their return confirms that those earlier chords were not interruptions but structural pillars.

cues.label: Flat-side intrusion in the coda
cues.vo_pre: A surprising chord is about to appear twice in succession, pulling briefly away from D major.
cues.vo_post: After a normal arrival on the dominant, the harmony shifts to a chord built on C, pointing toward F major. B flat in the top voice is the most prominent flat-side pitch in the entire coda. The flat world resurfaces even here, briefly, before D major pulls back.

cues.label: Registral summit
cues.vo_pre: The first violin is about to reach the highest pitch of the entire movement.
cues.vo_post: A six , two octaves above the A below middle C. The registral peak of the movement, arrived at through a long D major expansion. The answer at measure 181 is a mirror sweep, both violins arcing in opposite directions through a full D major chord. Summit and response in a single gesture.

cues.label: Chromatic cello descent and final dissolution
cues.vo_pre: The cello begins one last descent, and the texture strips away to almost nothing.
cues.vo_post: By measure 191, only the first violin and cello remain, stating D alone , no third, no fifth, just the root. And then measure 192 arrives. Not D major. A fully diminished seventh on B, containing F and A flat, the first and third of F minor. The movement ends not with resolution but with a threshold. The next movement begins before the silence can form.

outro.vo: The second movement ends where it refuses to arrive. The brightness of D major has dissolved into a four-note chord that belongs to no key and closes nothing. What that chord contains , F and A flat , are the opening pitches of F minor, the world of the first movement, the world about to return. Movement three begins immediately, attacca, with no gap, no breath. The question the second movement leaves open becomes the first sound of the third.
